newsitem.title: GERMANY: CDU's Repnik sees tax talks with SPD next week.
newsitem.headline: CDU's Repnik sees tax talks with SPD next week.

text.p: Hans-Peter Repnik, deputy parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said on Friday he expects tax reform talks with opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to resume next week.

"I can only hope that the SPD takes up our offer, that we come constructively, quickly and without delay to a tax reform (plan) that will lead to new jobs. I presume that we will have the first talks next week," Repnik said in a radio interview.
SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine said on Thursday his party would only return to the bargaining table if Kohl came up with fresh proposals to discuss, but Repnik said there would be no new proposals.
"We have already presented a completed concept to the public and the SPD," Repnik said.
"Now it is up to the SPD to say which of our proposals it is prepared to support and which not, so that we can come to concrete talks."
Finance Minister Theo Waigel is to present his legislative proposals for tax reform later on Friday. The plan is aimed at stimulating economic growth and boosting jobs.
The SPD boycotted a round of talks last Saturday in protest against the government's plan to curtail coal subsidies.
